niche_preference_profile: This user prefers interfaces that feel complete, structured, and easy to scan: populated screens with clear sectioning, balanced vertical distribution, and explicit labels/controls. They generally like light or airy layouts for settings and onboarding, but prefer darker, calmer, more focused treatment for critical modal/alert flows. Across most screens they favor concise copy, strong hierarchy, and visible primary actions, while rejecting sparse, unfinished, or overly cluttered compositions.

criteria.description: Prefers screens that feel fully populated, finished, and not placeholder-like, with multiple visible items and few empty areas.
Prefers obvious grouping into meaningful categories or sections, with structure that makes the content easy to understand at a glance.
Prefers layouts that distribute content evenly down the page and avoid large dead zones or awkward empty lower areas.
Prefers short, direct, task-focused text over verbose, promotional, or overly explanatory copy.
Prefers rows and controls that clearly signal what is tappable or adjustable, using consistent chevrons, toggles, and action patterns.
Prefers clear hierarchy through section headers, title prominence, and separation between content blocks so the page is easy to scan.
Prefers interfaces that minimize competing chrome, banners, and extra decorative elements so the main task stays focused.
Prefers concrete, task-oriented labels and status text that make options feel familiar, relevant, and immediately understandable.
Prefers a clearly visible primary action that stands out enough to guide the next step without feeling overly aggressive.
